title: Man admits Edmonton cops had to shoot him
article: A man who was shot by Edmonton police after waving a starter pistol at officers in a possible suicide-by-cop attempt owned up to his actions in court on Friday.

Interestingly, the 33 year old is the brother of one man who was shot dead by a police sniper in a standoff and a second man who is serving a life sentence for fatally shooting a Mountie during the same 2001 crime spree.
Dusty Sand pleaded guilty in Provincial Court to charges of possession of a weapon dangerous to the public peace, uttering death threats and carrying a concealed weapon.
Crown prosecutor Keith Nicholls told court police were called after Sand was overheard by a city bus driver talking on the phone about a "suicide by cop."

The bus driver pulled into the Westwood bus terminal, in the area of 118 Avenue and 106 Street, about 2 a.m. on Dec. 28, 2013, and exited the bus after seeing Sand sitting with an exposed knife beside him on the seat.

Two Edmonton Transit officers found Sand in front of the bus with the knife in his right hand and ordered him to put it down. He refused and told them he had a second weapon "that could kill you." Sand also told them that the RCMP had killed one of his brothers, said Nicholls.

When the female officer put her hand near her utility belt, Sand said: "I would never hurt a girl." He then pointed at the male officer and said: "You'll be dead before you reach me." He also told the pair that he would shoot them if they didn't tell a third transit officer to leave.
Police arrived and Sand then pulled out what was believed to be a small black firearm.

"Mr. Sand was agitated and was pacing back and forth with the weapon in his left hand, raised in a lateral sweeping motion," said Nicholls, adding that he refused to comply with orders to put down his weapons.
A police officer then shot Sand with a single round from a carbine, striking him in the right arm. He was arrested and treated in hospital for his minor wound.
The gun was determined to be a .22-calibre starter pistol.
Defence lawyer Jonathan Kerber said Sand was drunk and has a history of substance abuse and depression.
A psychiatric assessment was ordered and a sentencing hearing was scheduled for Dec. 12.
In December 2001, Robert Sand, his girlfriend Laurie Bell and his younger brother Danny left Edmonton and embarked on a crime spree across the Prairies.
After amassing a virtual armoury of weapons, the Sands and Bell were stopped by RCMP after running a stop sign on a highway near Russell, Manitoba.

Robert Sand opened fire on the police car and then pursued the frightened officers back to the RCMP detachment, where he rammed their car and then pumped four shotgun blasts into the passenger door, killing RCMP Const. Dennis Strongquill, a 52-year-old father of six.

Danny Sand was killed by a police sniper during a standoff at a Saskatchewan motel about 12 hours later and Bell and Robert Sand surrendered. Robert Sand was later convicted of first-degree murder and is serving a life sentence with no parole eligibility for 25 years. Bell was given 10 years after a jury convicted her of manslaughter.
